learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess learning skills that allow for lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.

syllabus_topics: Generalities. Importance and historical evolution. Classification of transports. Transport systems. Modes. Transport demand. Energy demand. Safety and environmental impact.
Introduction. Traffic engineering. Fundamental concepts. Traffic study variables. Fundamental traffic equation. Traffic capacity and service level of a road.
Types and characteristics. Performance. Vehicle systems. Safety. Dynamics.
Railway Electrification Systems. Railway Signaling. Telecommunications. Safety in operation and systems in tunnels and unique infrastructures.
Types, performance and components. Railway dynamics. Traction and braking systems. On-board systems.
Generalities. Main characteristics. Elements of an elevator. Regulations.
Advantages and limitations. Types. Hydraulic system.
Topic 10: Other means of vertical and inclined transport.
Drum winding elevators. Rack and pinion elevators. Screw elevators. Pneumatic elevators. Platforms with cabin. Stairlifts. Freight lifts.
assessment_rules: The continuous or progressive evaluation system consists of two tests throughout the semester, each covering a part of the subject and weighing 50% of the final grade. To pass any test or activity, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained. The overall grade in the ordinary call is the arithmetic mean of the grades obtained in each of the two parts, provided a minimum of 5 points has been achieved in each part. Students who have not passed a part in continuous evaluation will take an ordinary global exam for that specific part. The extraordinary global evaluation consists of a single written exam covering all course material, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 points to pass.
